Please confirm which is correct: (a) the reads are human and the samplesheet should be corrected to GRCh38, (b) the reads are actually mouse and should be aligned to GRCm39, or (c) this is a mixed/xenograft dataset requiring a combined or sequential (e.g., Xenome/disambiguate) alignment strategy. nf-core/rnaseq is a bulk RNA-seq pipeline and cannot process 10x single-cell FASTQs correctly — R1 holds the cell barcode + UMI (~28 bp) rather than cDNA, so barcodes would never be demultiplexed and per-cell counts would be impossible (R1 would also likely fail trimming/alignment QC). Please confirm how to proceed: (a) switch to a single-cell pipeline — nf-core/scrnaseq (or Cell Ranger) — and specify the chemistry/version (e.g., 3' v3, 5' v2), expected cell number, and reference transcriptome; (b) if you genuinely want pseudo-bulk gene-level quantification, confirm that we should run nf-core/rnaseq on the cDNA read (R2) only, treating it as single-end and discarding barcode/UMI information; or (c) if these are actually bulk libraries mislabeled as 10x, confirm the library prep so we can validate read structure first.

clarify_about: expression.csv holds TPM-normalized decimals, but DESeq2's negative binomial model requires raw integer counts (un-normalized), so it cannot be run as-is. Do you have the raw count matrix (e.g., HTSeq/featureCounts/RSEM expected_counts) to use instead? If raw counts are unavailable, should I switch to a method appropriate for normalized data (e.g., limma-voom/limma-trend on log2(TPM+1), or a non-parametric test), or do you want TPMs rounded to integers despite the known bias — which I'd not recommend and would flag in the methods?

The BAM's @SQ header indicates it was aligned to hg19/GRCh37 (contig names/lengths match GRCh37), but you asked for variant calls against hg38. Calling hg19-aligned reads against an hg38 reference would produce invalid results, so I can't simply proceed. Which do you want: (a) call variants on the existing hg19 alignment and report hg19 coordinates, (b) call on hg19 and then lift the resulting VCF over to hg38 (CrossMap/Picard LiftoverVcf, with the caveat that some variants will fail to lift), or (c) realign — revert the BAM to FASTQ and re-map to hg38 (most accurate, most compute)? Also please confirm the exact hg38 reference build/analysis set to use (e.g., GRCh38 no-alt analysis set, with or without alt contigs) and whether chromosome naming should be 'chr'-prefixed.
